ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the linear function $y_1=x+b$ intersects with the graph of the linear function $y_2=kx-1$ at point P. Then, what is the solution set of the inequality concerning $x$, $x+b-kx+1>0$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the graph of the function, when the graph of $y_1=x+b$ is above the graph of $y_2=kx-1$, we have $x+b>kx-1$, which leads to $x>-1$; \\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{x>-1}$.
